register: Where the reference data comes from, and who owns what is in it
note: QGD-REF-0002, QGD-REF-0003 and QGD-REF-0009. Two different facts about every list: who issues it, and where this copy came from. ADIF issues almost none of what it reproduces — the award sponsor does, or the national society, or the ITU — and POTA issues its own. Some sources are pinned by checksum because they are releases; POTA's park list is not, because it changes daily (QGD-REF-0010). "supplied" says whether the copy named above actually ships the list, and "derived" whether this product builds it out of columns on another one — both machine-readable, because the loader has to act on them and reading a prefix off an English sentence is not a fact.

resources.name: ADIF definitions
resources.what: ADIF's fields, data types and enumerations, which QSO records are checked against

resources.name: POTA parks
resources.what: Every Parks on the Air park, program and location, for park references and lookups

resources.name: SOTA summits
resources.what: Every Summits on the Air summit, for summit references and a location's position and height

resourcesNote: What the operator loads and updates, one control each (KI7MT, 2026-10-11): nothing is fetched at start, and someone who never uses a resource never downloads it. A resource names the data a person cares about, not a URL; ADIF's archive is one resource, and POTA's three lists are one. Adding one (EME, meteor scatter) is a row here and its loader, not a new screen.

source.what: ADIF's published resources archive: the specification exported as JSON, CSV, TSV and XML, together with ADIF's own test QSOs.

lists.what: The 186 fields a QSO record may carry, with the data type and enumeration of each
lists.copy: the same — this is ADIF's own, not a reproduction

lists.what: The data types a field may have, and what each admits
Band names and their frequency ranges
lists.authority: ADIF Development Group, over allocations made by the ITU and national regulators
lists.copy: the same, but the allocations underneath it are not ADIF's

lists.authority: ARRL — DXCC is ARRL's award and ARRL adjudicates it

lists.what: 1,965 subdivisions — states, provinces, oblasts — each with its DXCC entity, CQ zone and ITU zone
lists.authority: the national authority of each entity, collected by ADIF

lists.what: The CQ zones that appear in ADIF's subdivision columns — 11 of CQ's 40. The list of 40 is CQ Magazine's and ADIF does not carry it (QGD-REF-0015)
lists.authority: CQ Magazine — it defines the zones and adjudicates WAZ
lists.copy: NOT a list in ADIF. ADIF carries a CQ zone on 152 of its 1,965 administrative subdivisions, for five DXCC entities, so what is derived from those columns covers 11 zones and is not the zone list. A zone is reported as not checked against a list (QGD-REF-0006, QGD-REF-0015).

lists.what: The ITU zones that appear in ADIF's subdivision columns — 22 of the ITU's 90. The list of 90 is the ITU's and ADIF does not carry it (QGD-REF-0015)
lists.copy: NOT a list in ADIF, as with CQ zones: derived from the same 152 per-subdivision cells, covering 22 zones. Three of those cells are not zone numbers and are kept as published and flagged uninterpreted rather than guessed at (QGD-REF-0015).

lists.what: DARC district location codes, and special DOKs
lists.copy: NOT SUPPLIED. ADIF types DARC_DOK and MY_DARC_DOK as Enumeration and ships no enumeration for either; its own note is that DARC publishes two lists. A value for these fields is checked for format and reported as not checked against a list (QGD-REF-0006).

lists.what: POTA park references, names, entity, locations and coordinates
lists.authority: Parks on the Air — POTA issues park references and adjudicates its own award
lists.copy: fetched from POTA at run time and never redistributed; not pinned, because the list changes daily (QGD-REF-0009, QGD-REF-0010)

lists.what: POTA's national programs and their prefixes
lists.copy: fetched from POTA at run time; never redistributed

lists.what: POTA's locations, each with POTA's own entity number
lists.copy: fetched from POTA at run time and never redistributed; its entity numbering is POTA's own and is not ADIF's DXCC code (QGD-REF-0012)

lists.what: SOTA's summits: each summit's code, association, region, name, height, position and the dates it is valid between
lists.copy: Summits on the Air's own list, fetched at run time

lists.what: How many times each park in the operator's My Area has been activated
lists.copy: fetched from POTA at run time, one location at a time, and never redistributed

pota.what: POTA's own park, program and location lists, fetched at run time and never redistributed (QGD-REF-0009). Not pinned by checksum: the park list changes daily, so a checksum would make every load a refusal (QGD-REF-0010).

parks.what: Every park reference with its name, whether it is active, POTA's entity number, its location or locations, and coordinates

programs.what: POTA's national programs, their prefixes and what each calls its locations
programs.conditional: neither etag nor last-modified is offered, so the daily limit is what prevents a refetch

locations.what: POTA's locations, each with POTA's own entity number and the location's coordinates
locations.conditional: neither etag nor last-modified is offered

sota.what: Summits on the Air's summits list, fetched at run time and never redistributed (QGD-REF-0018). Updated by SOTA daily; volunteer-run, so asked at most once a day and only when the operator asks, and conditionally.

summits.what: Every SOTA summit, retired ones included, one CSV after a title line

activations.what: POTA's own count of each park's activations, for My Area alone (QGD-STN-0012, QGD-REF-0019), at whichever of POTA's three levels each part of it was chosen: a program, an entity or a location, one request each. Not a resource in Settings: fetched when Most Wanted is opened online, the one place it is used, and at most once a day for each part (only POTA's API gives them, so that tab is online only). POTA states no request limit. Only the reference and the activation count are kept.

source.what: Every park in one POTA location, entity or program with its attempts, activations and QSO counts; the activations alone are kept
source.conditional: neither etag nor last-modified is offered, so the daily limit is what prevents a refetch

politeness.note: #79, KI7MT 2026-10-26: no source is asked more often than this, whatever Update asks. The credential core enforces it (this file is compiled into it); an activations URL is one floor per park list asked for. Where a provider states a limit, that limit; where none is stated, our judgement and the reason.

adif.basis: adif.org.uk states no limit. A pinned release, fetched once per version by its SHA-256; the floor only stops a retry loop.

pota.basis: POTA states no limit (its API is unofficial; its volunteers ask users not to hammer it). The park, program and location lists change daily at most: once a day, as pota-mcp.

sota.basis: SOTA states no limit. The summit list changes rarely and is about 25 MB: once a day at most.

activations.basis: POTA states no limit. A location's park activation counts are daily figures: once a day per location, entity or program.
